## Keep wall ghosts consistent with the hydrostatic reference (`dynamics/wb-wall-clamp`) {#sec-ch11-wb}

<!-- PROVENANCE
pin: snapy@e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0
status: draft
-->

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
For gravity-driven x1 reconstruction, mirror pressure and density perturbations at physical non-outflow faces. The default reference continues density/pressure using owned cells.
Default: true.
Order: exact discrete operation or local derivation below; coupled solver order not measured.
:::

### Derivation

All states here are cell averages; $\chi=\rho/p$ has units $\mathrm{s^2\,m^{-2}}$.
Write the default reference smoothing with the notation-table binomial weights $B=(1,4,6,4,1)/16$.
On a uniform grid its unit sum and zero first moment reproduce linear data. Repeating the first owned
$\chi$ beyond a wall breaks that cancellation: a Taylor expansion has an uncancelled first-derivative term
of order $h$. Continuing from two owned cells cancels it.

Let owned cells start at index zero, let $l$ count continuation depth, and use positive owned values.
The implementation chooses

$$
\chi_{-l}=\begin{cases}
\chi_0(\chi_0/\chi_1)^l,&\chi_1>\chi_0,\\
\chi_0+l(\chi_0-\chi_1),&\chi_1\le\chi_0.
\end{cases}
$$ {#eq-ch11-wb-continuation}

`hydro_ref_x1_wall_rop` ([`hydro_ref_x1_impl.h:69-104`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_ref_x1_impl.h#L69-L104)) implements @eq-ch11-wb-continuation, with fallback to $\chi_0$ if the
computed value is not positive. The first branch linearly continues $\log\chi$, the second $\chi$.
Expanding the power branch about equal adjacent values gives the same constant and linear terms as the
second branch; the difference is $O(h^2)$ at fixed $l$. The binomial first moment then cancels the wall's
$O(h)$ error for smooth data on a uniform grid. This is a truncation argument, not a fitted solver order.
The reference construction is derived in the well-balanced chapter; the underlying note is
`docs/derivations/wb-ref-wall.md@e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0` section 4.
No historical measured values from that note are reused. C7 checks the binomial moments, the repeated-cell
linear bias and the first-order agreement of the two continuations symbolically.

The sweep subtracts $p_{\mathrm{ref}}$ and $\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}$, then mirrors the perturbations:

$$
\begin{aligned}
p'_{i-l}&=p'_{i+l-1},\\
\rho'_{i-l}&=\rho'_{i+l-1}.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch11-wb-parity}

`is_outflow` guards these fills in [`hydro_forward.cpp:287-343`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L287-L343), which implements @eq-ch11-wb-parity only at physical non-outflow
faces. If the cell state matches the discrete reference exactly, both perturbations vanish, their mirrors
vanish, and a constant-preserving reconstruction returns zero perturbation. Restoring matched reference
face values therefore adds no perturbation flux residual. The full pressure/gravity cancellation is the
well-balanced scheme's identity, not a consequence of parity alone. C7 checks zero-perturbation preservation.

The report-only checks are `src/snapy_report/ch11/boundary_check.py`; their current output is
`src/snapy_report/ch11/boundary_check.out`. They do not call a snapy kernel.

### Numerical method

The well-balanced x1 path requires nonzero x1 gravity, a pressure row and an EOS other than shallow water.
The old isentropic ghost revision calls are commented out. The optional mass-covariance path uses one-sided
density derivatives and odd corrected-velocity ghosts at the same physical non-outflow ends.
Without WB, the gravity path revises reconstructed face pairs instead. Default reference wall clamping
passes physical-face flags into the kernel; unlike perturbation mirroring, those flags do not exclude outflow.
The continuation requires owned neighbours; thin-block fallbacks belong to the reference kernel tests.

The optional reference variant uses `SNAP_WB_REF4`; `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` implies that variant.
Both environment switches default off. This section does not rederive their high-order stencils or assign
measured wall/seam convergence to them.

@fig-ch11-wb-stencil illustrates the operations, with labelled roles independent of colour.

```{python}

#| fig-alt: "Labelled schematic of the wb boundary operation; ghosts and owned cells have separate text labels."
```

: Implementation sites for wb. {#tbl-ch11-wb-code}

1. Select the gravity/pressure WB branch and construct its reference using physical-face flags. The anchor `wall_clamp` is in [`hydro.cpp:503-556`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro.cpp#L503-L556).
2. Subtract the reference and mirror only non-outflow physical-end perturbations. The anchor `is_outflow` is in [`hydro_forward.cpp:287-343`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L287-L343).
3. Apply selected mass-covariance wall treatment, reconstruct, and restore the reference; the non-WB path instead revises face pairs. The anchor `_revise_x1` is in [`hydro_forward.cpp:378-383`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L378-L383).

### Limits

The reference clamp still receives physical-face flags for outflow ([`hydro.cpp:503-556`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro.cpp#L503-L556)); it is incorrect to summarize
all WB wall operations as excluding outflow. An in-block periodic x1 callback can count as physical here while
`is_x1_wall` excludes its name ([`hydro.cpp:204-209`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro.cpp#L204-L209)). The two-resolution test assertion is not the three-resolution fitted
order required for a report measurement. Nonuniform-grid wall accuracy and outflow/implicit/WB combinations
remain unmeasured in this draft. The derivation is restricted to smooth uniform-grid data.

Untested switch combinations remain subject to @sec-ch12-matrix. No new CPU, CUDA or multi-rank solver result is claimed.
